fixture.name: travel
setup: graph-agents-cli create itinerary -o travel -y --skip-checks --registry ghcr.io/acme --auth-policy jwt
graph-agents-cli create flights-agent -o travel -y --skip-checks --registry ghcr.io/acme --auth-policy jwt
graph-agents-cli create hotels-agent -o travel -y --skip-checks --registry ghcr.io/acme --auth-policy jwt

prompt: travel/ holds three agents made with graph-agents-cli: itinerary, flights-agent and hotels-agent. itinerary should ask flights-agent and hotels-agent for the signed-in user. It must never approve anything at hotels-agent for them: people approve their bookings there themselves. Wire the three as one system for the dev environment, described in a file in travel/ that the team can review and re-apply. Our identity provider is https://id.example.org; its token endpoint in dev is http://id.identity.svc.cluster.local/token.

checks.expr: (lambda names: bool(names.get('flights-agent')) and bool(names.get('hotels-agent')) and {names.get('flights-agent'), names.get('hotels-agent')} <= {a for a, _ in (lambda ag, names: [((c if isinstance(c, str) else c.get('agent')), ('relay' if isinstance(c, str) else c.get('approvals', 'relay'))) for v in ag.values() if str((v or {}).get('project', '')).strip('./') == 'itinerary' for c in ((v or {}).get('calls') or [])])(get(data, 'agents') or {}, names)})({str((v or {}).get('project', '')).strip('./'): k for k, v in (get(data, 'agents') or {}).items()})
checks.why: graph-agents-system.yaml (`graph-agents-cli system`) names each agent's project and the agents it calls; `system apply` writes both sides of every edge from it

checks.expr: (lambda names: dict((lambda ag, names: [((c if isinstance(c, str) else c.get('agent')), ('relay' if isinstance(c, str) else c.get('approvals', 'relay'))) for v in ag.values() if str((v or {}).get('project', '')).strip('./') == 'itinerary' for c in ((v or {}).get('calls') or [])])(get(data, 'agents') or {}, names)).get(names.get('hotels-agent')) == 'deny' and dict((lambda ag, names: [((c if isinstance(c, str) else c.get('agent')), ('relay' if isinstance(c, str) else c.get('approvals', 'relay'))) for v in ag.values() if str((v or {}).get('project', '')).strip('./') == 'itinerary' for c in ((v or {}).get('calls') or [])])(get(data, 'agents') or {}, names)).get(names.get('flights-agent')) == 'relay')({str((v or {}).get('project', '')).strip('./'): k for k, v in (get(data, 'agents') or {}).items()})
checks.why: an edge whose caller must never approve at the called agent is `{agent: NAME, approvals: deny}`; a bare name relays the person's approvals

checks.expr: sum(1 for a in (get(data, 'apis') or {}).values() if isinstance(a, dict) and a.get('protocol') == 'a2a' and any(isinstance(d, dict) and d.get('a2a_operation') == 'approve' for d in (a.get('denied_operations') or []))) == 1
checks.why: the caller's policy denies messages that approve at hotels-agent (written by `system apply` from the edge)
`graph-agents-cli system check` finds what keeps the agents from calling each other; fix every error it reports

reference: Write travel/graph-agents-system.yaml: version 1, agents itinerary (project itinerary, calls flights and {agent: hotels, approvals: deny}), flights (project flights-agent), hotels (project hotels-agent); identity issuer https://id.example.org with token_url for dev; environments dev. Then `graph-agents-cli system check`, `system apply` (--dry-run first): peers in itinerary at each agent's A2A mount /a2a/app (exchange, audiences flights and hotels; the hotels peer denies approve messages), and in the called agents AUTH_JWT_AUDIENCE, AUTH_ALLOWED_ACTORS itinerary and appUrl. Set AUTH_JWT_ISSUER https://id.example.org in both called agents' values-dev.yaml (SC04) until `system check --env dev` exits 0. A bare `hotels` in calls relays the person's approvals instead of denying them.
